title: The configuration file and the handful of parameters worth touching

videos.script: A PostgreSQL server reads one file of settings, and the last value it reads for a name is the one it uses. {{file}} That file has eight hundred lines, and twenty-five of them do anything. The rest are comments. So the first job is reading what is really set, and asking the server what it is really using. Those are two different questions. {{settings}} Then you change something. Some settings apply when you reload, and nobody notices. Others need a restart, and every connection is cut. {{reload}} You will make a typo on purpose, and see why a reload forgives it and a restart does not. There is also a file the server writes for itself, and it beats yours without saying so. {{auto}} Then the other file: the short list that decides who may connect at all. You will read it line by line, break one line, and read the refusal in the log. {{hba}} Last, the dozen settings worth touching, and the few you never relax. {{handful}} Every change in this lesson is undone at the end, so the next lesson starts where this one did. {{title}}
